thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SLO breach: dedicated-pool-usw2 (model-raven-3b) p99 streaming stalls > 8s. Auto-escalation threshold hit. Queue depth 4200, warmup backlog building. Paging oncall.

oncall_sam: I'm on it. Paging ENG-SRE and runtime. Any immediate customer reports? @anya-support?

anya-support: A few customers reported timeouts from in-app chat. Diego (CS) said one enterprise reported degraded UX and opened a ticket. No widespread error 5xx though — mostly long tails / stalled streaming.

maya-eng-sre: Seeing the same in telemetry. p95 jumped from ~180ms to 2.6s over the last 6m, p99 at 9.2s. Streaming stalls show long tail on last-token flush. Heatmap attached: high concentration on dedicated pool slots 12-18.

leon-eng-runtime: Autoscaler logs show scale-up handshake lag ~75s for new GPUs to become warm. Warmup jobs queueing; handshake failures intermittently at 3%. Looks like warmup parallelism was capped yesterday after a config change (nina, any recent policy change?)

nina-eng-platform: I rolled a conservative warmup parallelism knob in the autoscaler policy last night to reduce spot volatility. It lowered cold-start cost but obviously reduces burst capacity. Reverting is possible but want safe plan.

oncall_sam: Ok immediate plan: (1) divert traffic for highest-latency customers to hosted fallback route; (2) temporarily raise warmup parallelism for dedicated pools; (3) enable overflow to quantized-variant (raven-3b-q4) for non-critical routes. Who can run the console toggles?

leon-eng-runtime: I can flip warmup parallelism and enable overflow. Will also push a rapid kernel-level metric to monitor KV-cache coldpath rates. Preparing commands.

maya-eng-sre: While leon does changes, I recommend we throttle large batched requests at the edge to reduce queue amplification — add a per-customer concurrent request cap for 2m.

ops-bot: runbook check: incident type = "capacity-saturation". Suggested mitigations: increase warmup parallelism, enable fallback shunt, apply per-customer rate-limit. Escalation to platform after 15m if not recovered.

leon-eng-runtime: Running patch now.

```bash
# increase warmup parallelism for dedicated-pool-usw2
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/v1/pools/usw2/dedicated/config -d '{"warmup_parallelism":8}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****'

# enable overflow to quantized variant for non-streaming routes
curl -X POST https://console.redwood/api/v1/routing/overflow -d '{"target":"raven-3b-q4","selector":"!streaming"}'
```

leon-eng-runtime: Warmup parallelism set to 8 (from 2). Overflow rule applied. Watching metrics.

maya-eng-sre: Implemented per-customer concurrent cap of 3 for heavy customers. That should reduce queue amplification. Patch id: patch/3481-throttle.

oncall_sam: Any immediate improvement?

maya-eng-sre: p95 dropping to ~650ms after 90s. p99 down from 9.2s to 3.7s in current window. Queue depth trending down: 4200 -> 900.

anya-support: Diego (CS) confirmed the main enterprise sees latency improving but still some residual stalls on long streaming sessions.

leon-eng-runtime: I see warm nodes coming online; handshake failures gone. Warmup completion rate increased. KV cache coldpath rate still elevated for ~3m — we'll let cache settle.

oncall_sam: Good. Notify customers and keep on watch. Any risk from reverting the conservative knob Nina set? Nina, is warmup_parallelism=8 safe for this cluster?

nina-eng-platform: 8 should be fine short-term. We'll need to monitor GPU utilization and preemption risk. I'll keep an eye. Suggest we roll back to 4 in 30m if stable.

maya-eng-sre: Noted. Also creating an alert for streaming-tail p99 > 4s with a dedupe window to avoid noisy paging.

diego-cs: Sending status to impacted customers: "We've applied temporary routing and capacity changes to reduce latency—service is recovering; further updates in 30m." Will escalate only if materially impacted.

oncall_sam: Final quick root-cause hypothesis: conservative warmup parallelism + sudden multi-customer burst (batch amplification) -> autoscaler handshake lag -> queue backlog -> streaming tail stalls. Mitigations applied: warmup_parallelism increase, overflow to quantized model, per-customer throttle.

maya-eng-sre: Short-term impact: reduced p99 from 9.2s -> ~3.2-3.8s and queues dropped. Long-tail recovery still ongoing. Customer impact: ~7 customers saw degraded streaming UX; 2 had support tickets opened. No data plane errors.

nina-eng-platform: Next actions: (1) schedule policy review to tune warmup parallelism defaults and burst profiles; (2) add autoscaler handshake telemetry to the incident dashboard; (3) evaluate adaptive warmup that can opportunistically pre-warm on predicted bursts.

leon-eng-runtime: I'll follow up with a postmortem doc with timeline and logs. Dumped relevant logs to /sre/incident-3481234567/logs and will attach perf snapshots.

ops-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. If any regression in next 30m, page oncall.

oncall_sam: Thanks all. Keeping this thread open for 30m. If anything new shows, post here. Otherwise we'll convert to postmortem notes.

maya-eng-sre: Adding a small TODO: ensure overflow rules exclude high-security customers (no fallback for private deployments). We excluded them in the rule but want explicit tests.

diego-cs: Noted. I'll follow up with the impacted enterprise with a timeline and link to postmortem once ready.

-- end of thread --
